subject: Latency incident recap & QBR-ready action handoff
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident INF-5231 — elevated tail latency for hosted inference (06/29 22:05 UTC)

Team,

Quick incident summary: between 22:05 and 22:27 UTC on 2027-06-29 we observed a spike in 99th-percentile latency for hosted text-generation routes serving model-xl-2. Impacted customers: ~12 active production tenants (total token throughput reduced ~18% during window). SLOs: 99th < 600ms; observed peaks up to ~1.9s. Root cause (preliminary): a regression in the KV cache eviction path combined with a degraded kernel selection path on a small subset of instances after yesterday's runtime patch.

Timeline (concise):
- 22:05 UTC: alert triggered — P99 above threshold on region-us-west-2
- 22:07 UTC: automated fallback routing engaged (migrated ~40% of in-flight requests to warm pool)
- 22:10 UTC: mitigation — forced cache TTL reset rolled to affected shard group
- 22:18 UTC: latency trending down, routing restored gradually
- 22:27 UTC: incident declared resolved; monitoring to confirm

Immediate customer outreach: we sent targeted messages to impacted account contacts (Acme Platform notified). I've opened JIRA INF-5231 and uploaded the raw traces and flamegraphs. Next steps I'm working on: full RCA write-up, patch candidate to KV eviction heuristics, and a small runtime rollback if patch validation fails.

Attachments: latency-graphs.png (summary), SLO slices available in the attached CSV.

Jonas
Senior SRE

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident INF-5231 — latency incident recap & action items

On Thu, Jun 30, 2027 at 9:12 AM, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team,
> 
> Quick incident summary: between 22:05 and 22:27 UTC on 2027-06-29 we observed...

Thanks Jonas — good concise timeline. For the exec audience and QBR I drafted a short two-page postmortem and a one-slide operational impact summary (attached as postmortem-draft.pdf). This message consolidates the immediate asks and owners so we can fold them into the QBR pack by EOD Friday.

Executive summary (for slides):
- What happened: transient regression in KV cache eviction combined with kernel selection fallback path -> P99 latency spike to 1.9s for ~22 minutes.
- Customer impact: ~12 tenants, targeted degradation; no data loss; fallbacks reduced severity.
- Business impact: estimated 0.4% reduction in billable token throughput for the hour; one customer (Acme) flagged for escalation to sales/CS.

Action items / owners / requested due dates:
1) Finalize RCA & remediation plan — Owner: Jonas Weber — due 2027-07-02 EOD.
2) Patch validation pipeline test (small canary run) — Owner: Hannah Schmitt — due 2027-07-03 midday.
3) QBR slide + one-line customer impact blurb — Owner: Marissa Cole (I'll draft) — due 2027-07-02 COB.
4) Customer outreach follow-up to Acme (CS + Sales) — Owner: Maria Lopez (Acme) + Vivek to approve messaging — target 2027-07-01.
5) Add compensating monitoring rule for cache-eviction anomalies — Owner: Platform Monitoring — JIRA INF-5231-2 — due 2027-07-07.

Notes for QBR: please keep the customer quote neutral (we confirmed degraded experience; no SLA credit requested yet). Vivek — recommend we include the incident as one line in the ops QBR with the mitigation timeline, and call out the corrective action that reduces recurrence risk.

Marissa
Director, Ops Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jun 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident INF-5231 — QBR framing and OKR implications

Thanks for the clear draft, Marissa. A couple notes from leadership lens:

1) QBR placement: include a dedicated 30-second slide under Reliability (ops block). Slide should state impact, root cause, and a single mitigation metric we're tracking (time-to-detect and recurrence probability).

2) OKR tie-ins: this incident maps to Objective: "Improve inference platform resilience" with the following measurable KR candidates — reduce P99 incident recurrence window to <1/month by end of Q3 and add automated eviction anomaly detection with an SLO of mean-time-to-detect <3 minutes. Please ensure the final RCA includes the proposed KR and a realistic implementation timeline.

3) Customer comms: approve the neutral outreach to Acme but ask CS to mention we're investigating possible SLA credit only if impacts persist after remediation. We should avoid proactively promising credits.

4) Credits / SLAs decision authority: finance + legal must be looped if Acme requests credits. Hannah, can you pre-open the support checklist for such requests so we don't delay?

If the RCA is done by 07/02 and validation on 07/03 looks good, we can include a short "Next 30 days" remedial plan slide in the QBR pack to show concrete progress. Ping me after Jonas posts the RCA.

Vivek
VP, Reliability & Product Ops

- Support checklist: opened INF-5231-SUPP to pre-clear finance/legal steps if Acme asks for credit.

I'll report back after the canary run.

Hannah
